description: We are building a health monitor for astronauts on long missions. It turns vitals like oxygen, heart rate, sleep, stress and radiation into one simple status, explains the risk, and recommends a countermeasure such as an exercise or recovery routine. A detailed view gives the medical chief every vital and trend, and the app is designed to work offline.
summary: AstroGuard is a tool for monitoring astronauts’ health and aiding decision making throughout missions. This was implemented using a React/Vite front-end with separate Astronaut and Medical Chief dashboards and a back-end using an Express server to provide role-based security. The health of astronauts were assessed using a Python FastAPI engine which scores astronauts on the 11 health domains including stress, bone and muscles. This provides deterministic health scoring, triage alerts, suggested countermeasures and long term forecasts for bones and muscles. To keep health as a priority, if there is no SIGNAL from any sensors it will show as NO SIGNAL. If any result comes up as WATCH or ALERT it will not show as FINE. An example 5 day mission with 4 simulated astronauts has been created to demonstrate how the tool works. This helps crews and flight surgeons identify health risks quickly and take action. As missions are getting longer such as going to the Moon and Mars it is vital to have proactive and autonomous systems in place for health. All of the data is simulated meaning this is just a demonstration tool.
details:
Overview: This is a health monitoring tool for astronauts. It monitors 11 key aspects of their health: Blood Pressure, SpO2, Body Temp, Heart Rate, Sleep, Stress, Hydration, Nutrition, Radiation, Bone Loss and Muscle Loss. These are all the main threats to health during long duration space travel. A Python backend scores them on a scale of 0-100 to give an interpretable "readiness" score. It also triages them into FINE/CAUTION/DANGER and suggests mitigation strategies like exercise, hydration and sleep. Each astronaut has their own health overview but there is also a "Medical Chief" page for the flight surgeon to monitor the whole crew's health. The health monitoring tool was demonstrated using a 5 day mission scenario showing the tool detecting health decline, a critical incident and partial recovery.

Benefits: During a mission to the moon/mars the crew won't have easy access to medical support. Using this tool will help detect issues early and triage them quickly. The astronauts can also view their own health data. All of the scores show what parameters contributed to the score.

Tools: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, TailwindCSS and Three.js for the 3D orbital view. An Express backend for authentication and role checking. A Python health score system using NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, FastAPI. Firebase/Firestore (optional). We implemented unit tests in Python as well as security and integration tests.

Creativity: The tool was designed to be fail-safe. If there isn't any data coming through from sensors it will say "NO SIGNAL". For anything that comes up as WATCH it will not be marked as FINE. If a vital sign comes back as critical it will say DANGER. If they report high stress it won't average out. We have a backup in TypeScript so the dashboard still works if the Python service goes down. The live ECG monitoring, 3D orbital view and emergency alert modal makes the demonstration easy to understand.

Considerations:

Data Privacy: Data is only visible to the astronaut and the flight surgeon.

Security: Signed session cookies, Role Checking on all health routes, Rate limiting, Audit logging and the Python backend was only on loopback.

Transparent: All the data from the crew is faked. The cut-offs are just part of the prototype. This is not a medical device and is not certified/validated by NASA. We referenced topics from the NASA Human Research Program.

Repeatable: The scores are all deterministic and the demo scenario is seeded.
